data.title: mTOR kinase structure, mechanism and regulation
data.authors: Yang H; Rudge DG; Koos JD; Vaidialingam B; Yang HJ; Pavletich NP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Solved the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase itself. Revealed why the active site is so hard to reach - it sits in a deep recess guarded by the FRB domain, which acts as a 'gatekeeper' letting substrates in. This structure explains at the atomic level exactly how FKBP12-rapamycin blocks access, and why activating cancer mutations cluster where they do.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), a phosphoinositide 3-kinase-related protein kinase, controls cell growth in response to nutrients and growth factors and is frequently deregulated in cancer. Here we report co-crystal structures of a complex of truncated mTOR and mammalian lethal with SEC13 protein 8 (mLST8) with an ATP transition state mimic and with ATP-site inhibitors. The structures reveal an intrinsically active kinase conformation, with catalytic residues and a catalytic mechanism remarkably similar to canonical protein kinases.

extracted_findings.effect: Co-crystal structures reveal mTOR's intrinsically active kinase and how ATP-site inhibitors bind
